import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
import numpy as np
from matplotlib.patches import FancyArrowPatch, Ellipse

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 5), dpi=300)

# --- Data (D076 protocol values) ---
data = {
    'SFT baseline':    (0.8013, 0.4049, 'o',  '#808080', 130),
    's42':             (0.8175, 0.4517, '*',  '#009E73', 120),
    's43':             (0.8063, 0.4601, '*',  '#009E73', 120),
    's44':             (0.8050, 0.4621, '*',  '#009E73', 120),
    's45':             (0.8174, 0.4514, '*',  '#009E73', 120),
    'GRPO QLoRA':      (0.8504, 0.0138, 'X',  '#D55E00', 150),
    'DPO 1ep':         (0.8088, 0.4034, 's',  '#CC79A7', 120),
}

# GRPO bf16 training trajectory (step 30/50/70/100)
grpo_bf16_traj = [
    (0.806, 0.434, 'step 30'),
    (0.802, 0.428, 'step 50'),
    (0.810, 0.434, 'step 70'),
    (0.809, 0.455, 'step 100'),
]

# DPO 3ep: evi_f1=0.8403 from pre-D076 eval, shown as hollow marker
dpo_3ep = (0.8403, 0.3429)

# --- Plot main data points ---
for label, (x, y, marker, color, ms) in data.items():
    ax.scatter(x, y, marker=marker, c=color, s=ms, edgecolors='k',
               linewidths=0.5, zorder=5)

# --- GRPO bf16 trajectory (connected triangles) ---
for i, (x, y, step_label) in enumerate(grpo_bf16_traj):
    ax.scatter(x, y, marker='^', c='#E69F00', s=90, edgecolors='k',
               linewidths=0.5, zorder=5)
    if i > 0:
        px, py, _ = grpo_bf16_traj[i - 1]
        ax.annotate('', xy=(x, y), xytext=(px, py),
                    arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#E69F00',
                                    lw=1.2, linestyle='--', alpha=0.7))

# --- DPO 3ep (hollow marker, pre-D076 eval) ---
ax.scatter(dpo_3ep[0], dpo_3ep[1], marker='s', facecolors='none',
           edgecolors='#CC79A7', s=120, linewidths=1.5, zorder=5)

# --- Annotations (manually tuned offsets to avoid overlap) ---
label_cfg = {
    'SFT baseline':  (-8, -14, 9),
    'GRPO QLoRA':    (-12, 14, 9),
    'DPO 1ep':       (10, -10, 9),
}

for label, (x, y, marker, color, ms) in data.items():
    if label not in label_cfg:
        continue
    ox, oy, fs = label_cfg[label]
    ha = 'left' if ox > 0 else ('center' if abs(ox) < 15 else 'right')
    ax.annotate(label, (x, y), textcoords='offset points', xytext=(ox, oy),
                fontsize=fs, ha=ha, va='center', zorder=6)

# DPO 3ep label (hollow point)
ax.annotate('DPO 3ep†', (dpo_3ep[0], dpo_3ep[1]),
            textcoords='offset points', xytext=(10, 4),
            fontsize=9, ha='left', va='center', zorder=6)

# GRPO bf16 trajectory label
ax.text(0.793, 0.425, 'GRPO bf16', fontsize=8.5, color='#E69F00',
        fontweight='bold', fontstyle='italic', ha='right', va='bottom')
# Step labels for first and last
ax.annotate('s30', (grpo_bf16_traj[0][0], grpo_bf16_traj[0][1]),
            textcoords='offset points', xytext=(-14, -8),
            fontsize=7.5, color='#E69F00', ha='right')
ax.annotate('s100', (grpo_bf16_traj[3][0], grpo_bf16_traj[3][1]),
            textcoords='offset points', xytext=(10, 8),
            fontsize=7.5, color='#E69F00', ha='left')
# Trajectory character label
ax.text(0.793, 0.415, 'mild, non-monotonic', fontsize=7.5, color='#E69F00',
        fontstyle='italic', ha='right', va='top', alpha=0.85)

# --- DPO decay arrow (1ep -> 3ep) ---
ax.annotate('', xy=(dpo_3ep[0], dpo_3ep[1]), xytext=(0.8088, 0.4034),
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#CC79A7', lw=1.5,
                            linestyle='--'))
ax.text(0.835, 0.382, 'gradual\ndecay', fontsize=8.5, color='#CC79A7',
        ha='center', va='center', fontstyle='italic')

# --- Catastrophic decoupling annotation ---
ax.annotate('catastrophic\ndecoupling', xy=(0.8504, 0.0138),
            xytext=(0.838, 0.08),
            fontsize=9, color='#D55E00', fontweight='bold',
            ha='center', va='bottom',
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#D55E00', lw=1.2))

# --- RSFT region ellipse ---
rsft_pts = np.array([
    [0.8175, 0.4517],
    [0.8063, 0.4601],
    [0.8050, 0.4621],
    [0.8174, 0.4514],
])
cx, cy = rsft_pts.mean(axis=0)
w = (rsft_pts[:, 0].max() - rsft_pts[:, 0].min()) * 2.2
h = (rsft_pts[:, 1].max() - rsft_pts[:, 1].min()) * 3.5
ellipse = Ellipse((cx, cy), w, h, angle=0, facecolor='#009E73', alpha=0.10,
                  edgecolor='#009E73', linewidth=1.0, linestyle='-', zorder=2)
ax.add_patch(ellipse)
ax.text(0.8115, 0.482, 'RSFT CED\n(4 seeds)', fontsize=9, color='#009E73',
        fontweight='bold', fontstyle='italic', ha='center', va='bottom',
        linespacing=0.85)

# --- SFT baseline horizontal line ---
ax.axhline(y=0.4049, color='#808080', linestyle=':', linewidth=1.0, alpha=0.5,
           zorder=1)
ax.text(0.858, 0.408, 'SFT baseline', fontsize=7.5, color='#808080',
        va='bottom', ha='right', fontstyle='italic', alpha=0.7)

# --- Footnote for hollow DPO 3ep ---
ax.text(0.78, -0.04, '† pre-D076 eval protocol',
        fontsize=7, color='#666666', fontstyle='italic',
        transform=ax.get_xaxis_transform())

# --- Decoupling direction arrow (diagonal) ---
ax.annotate('', xy=(0.850, 0.05), xytext=(0.795, 0.46),
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#555555', lw=1.5,
                            linestyle='--', alpha=0.5))
ax.text(0.837, 0.24, 'Optimization\npressure', fontsize=8.5, color='#555555',
        ha='center', va='center', rotation=-55, fontstyle='italic', alpha=0.6)

# --- Legend ---
legend_elements = [
    plt.Line2D([0], [0], marker='o', color='w', markerfacecolor='#808080',
               markeredgecolor='k', markersize=8, label='SFT'),
    plt.Line2D([0], [0], marker='*', color='w', markerfacecolor='#009E73',
               markeredgecolor='k', markersize=10, label='RSFT CED'),
    plt.Line2D([0], [0], marker='^', color='w', markerfacecolor='#E69F00',
               markeredgecolor='k', markersize=8, label='GRPO bf16 (trajectory)'),
    plt.Line2D([0], [0], marker='X', color='w', markerfacecolor='#D55E00',
               markeredgecolor='k', markersize=8, label='GRPO QLoRA'),
    plt.Line2D([0], [0], marker='s', color='w', markerfacecolor='#CC79A7',
               markeredgecolor='k', markersize=8, label='DPO (filled=D076)'),
    plt.Line2D([0], [0], marker='s', color='w', markerfacecolor='w',
               markeredgecolor='#CC79A7', markersize=8, label='DPO (hollow=pre-D076)'),
]
ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc='lower left', fontsize=8,
          framealpha=0.9, edgecolor='#cccccc')

# --- Axes ---
ax.set_xlabel('Evi-F1 (Evidence Quality)', fontsize=12)
ax.set_ylabel('Rel-F1 (Extraction Performance)', fontsize=12)
ax.set_xlim(0.78, 0.86)
ax.set_ylim(0.0, 0.52)
ax.tick_params(labelsize=10)
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.2, color='#999999', linestyle='-', linewidth=0.5)

# --- Clean up spines ---
for spine in ['top', 'right']:
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)

fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig('/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0513_6/projects/faith-evidence-ie/figures/paper/fig_spectrum.pdf',
            bbox_inches='tight', dpi=300)
fig.savefig('/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0513_6/projects/faith-evidence-ie/figures/paper/fig_spectrum.png',
            bbox_inches='tight', dpi=300)
print('Done. PDF and PNG saved.')

dpo_3ep = (0.8484, 0.3145)

# --- Plot main data points ---
for label, (x, y, marker, color, ms) in data.items():

# --- GRPO bf16 trajectory (connected triangles) ---
for i, (x, y, step_label) in enumerate(grpo_bf16_traj):

for label, (x, y, marker, color, ms) in data.items():
    if label not in label_cfg:
        continue
    ox, oy, fs = label_cfg[label]

        fontweight='bold', fontstyle='italic', ha='right', va='bottom')

            fontsize=9, color='#D55E00', fontweight='bold',
            ha='center', va='bottom',
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#D55E00', lw=1.2))

# --- RSFT region ellipse ---
rsft_pts = np.array([

    [0.8174, 0.4514],

h = (rsft_pts[:, 1].max() - rsft_pts[:, 1].min()) * 3.5
ellipse = Ellipse((cx, cy), w, h, angle=0, facecolor='#009E73', alpha=0.10,

ax.text(0.8115, 0.482, 'RSFT CED\n(4 seeds)', fontsize=9, color='#009E73',

                            linestyle='--', alpha=0.5))
ax.text(0.837, 0.24, 'Optimization\npressure', fontsize=8.5, color='#555555',
        ha='center', va='center', rotation=-55, fontstyle='italic', alpha=0.6)

# --- Legend ---
legend_elements = [

               markeredgecolor='k', markersize=10, label='RSFT CED'),
    plt.Line2D([0], [0], marker='^', color='w', markerfacecolor='#E69F00',
               markeredgecolor='k', markersize=8, label='GRPO bf16 (trajectory)'),
    plt.Line2D([0], [0], marker='X', color='w', markerfacecolor='#D55E00',
               markeredgecolor='k', markersize=8, label='GRPO QLoRA'),

               markeredgecolor='k', markersize=8, label='DPO (1ep → 3ep)'),

ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc='lower left', fontsize=8,
          framealpha=0.9, edgecolor='#cccccc')

# --- Axes ---
ax.set_xlabel('Evi-F1 (Evidence Quality)', fontsize=12)

# --- Clean up spines ---
for spine in ['top', 'right']:

fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig('/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0513_6/projects/faith-evidence-ie/figures/paper/fig_spectrum.pdf',

fig.savefig('/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0513_6/projects/faith-evidence-ie/figures/paper/fig_spectrum.png',

print('Done. PDF and PNG saved.')

Cross-family validation on LLaMA-3.1-8B confirms these patterns. All three RSFT seeds (55.87--57.14) exceed all three SFT seeds (48.02--53.84), yielding complete pairwise seed separation (Cohen's $d{=}2.58$) and 4.6$\times$ variance compression (std 2.92pp $\to$ 0.64pp). The SFT seed lottery is starkest at s44 (48.02 Ign-F1, 24.4\% truncation, elevated Evi-F1 85\%), a degenerate outcome that RSFT eliminates entirely (s44: 55.87). This robustness extends to inference-time format changes: LLaMA SFT models evaluated without evidence at 1024 tokens suffer 38--42\% truncation with Ign-F1 collapsing to ${\sim}$0.33 (s43/s44), while RSFT models truncate only 18--19\% with stable performance (55.41$\pm$0.13pp), indicating that CED filtering selects for compact output structure.

For RSFT models, the inference-time evidence tax (same model evaluated with vs.\ without evidence output) preserves the benefit direction at 1.7B ($-$7.75pp, confirmed with 2048-token no-evidence evaluation that rules out truncation). At 4B, where the training-time tax is approximately neutral (+0.25$\pm$0.47pp; Appendix~\ref{sec:training_tax}), the RSFT inference-time tax is similarly small (+0.94pp). At 8B, the tax reverses to a benefit ($-$0.78pp), and at 14B the benefit is largest ($-$4.54pp). RSFT thus maintains or improves extraction quality with evidence across the Qwen3 family. LLaMA-3.1-8B RSFT shows a larger inference-time evidence benefit ($-$2.17$\pm$0.76pp, three-seed mean, vs.\ $-$0.78pp for Qwen3-8B), confirming that both performance gains and training reliability generalize across model families.

The effect of RSFT on inference-time evidence dependence is heterogeneous. At 1.7B, RSFT maintains strong evidence benefit ($-$5.43pp\textsuperscript{$\ddagger$}), comparable to SFT ($-$4.86pp). At 4B, RSFT introduces a mild evidence cost (+1.51pp), the only Qwen3 scale with a positive RSFT test tax. Within the Qwen3 family at $\geq$8B, RSFT approaches evidence neutrality, with test tax magnitudes below 1pp. Cross-architecture, LLaMA-3.1-8B shows partial compression: SFT tax of $-$4.94pp reduces to $-$1.74pp under RSFT, consistent with the cross-family variation observed in SFT evidence tax (Appendix~\ref{sec:training_tax}).

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# Corrected values per Reviewer verification (2026-05-23)
# Inference-time evidence tax = no_evi - with_evi (positive = evidence hurts)
# Re-DocRED test set, RSFT models
models = ['Qwen3\n1.7B', 'Qwen3\n4B', 'Qwen3\n8B', 'LLaMA\n3.1-8B', 'Qwen3\n14B']
tax_values = [-5.43, 1.65, -0.91, -1.74, 0.77]
# Error bars (std) — only where >=2 seeds available
# 4B: 3 seeds (s42=+1.51, s43=+1.99, s44=+1.46), std=0.29
# Others: single seed or need verification
tax_errors = [0, 0.29, 0, 0, 0]
n_seeds = [1, 3, 1, 1, 1]  # seed count for annotations

# Okabe-Ito colors: blue for negative (evidence helps), orange for positive (evidence hurts)
colors = ['#0072B2' if v < 0 else '#E69F00' for v in tax_values]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5), dpi=300)

x = np.arange(len(models))
bars = ax.bar(x, tax_values, width=0.6, color=colors, edgecolor='k', linewidth=0.5, zorder=3)

# Error bars (only where std > 0)
for i, (val, err) in enumerate(zip(tax_values, tax_errors)):
    if err > 0:
        ax.errorbar(i, val, yerr=err, fmt='none', ecolor='k', capsize=4, capthick=1.0,
                    linewidth=1.0, zorder=4)

# Zero baseline
ax.axhline(y=0, color='k', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.8, alpha=0.5, zorder=2)

# Value annotations on bars
for i, (val, err, ns) in enumerate(zip(tax_values, tax_errors, n_seeds)):
    sign = '+' if val > 0 else ''
    label = f'{sign}{val:.2f}pp'
    if ns == 1 and i == len(models) - 1:  # 14B
        label += '\n($n$=1)'
    y_offset = 0.25 if val >= 0 else -0.25
    va = 'bottom' if val >= 0 else 'top'
    if err > 0:
        y_pos = val + err + 0.15 if val >= 0 else val - 0.15
        va = 'bottom' if val >= 0 else 'top'
    else:
        y_pos = val + y_offset
    ax.text(i, y_pos, label, ha='center', va=va, fontsize=8.5, fontweight='bold')

# Axes
ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels(models, fontsize=9)
ax.set_ylabel('Evidence Tax (pp)', fontsize=11)
ax.set_ylim(-7.0, 4.0)
ax.tick_params(axis='y', labelsize=9)
ax.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.2, color='#999999', linestyle='-', linewidth=0.5, zorder=1)

# Legend
from matplotlib.patches import Patch
legend_elements = [
    Patch(facecolor='#0072B2', edgecolor='k', linewidth=0.5, label='Evidence helps (negative tax)'),
    Patch(facecolor='#E69F00', edgecolor='k', linewidth=0.5, label='Evidence hurts (positive tax)'),
]
ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc='lower left', fontsize=8, framealpha=0.9, edgecolor='#cccccc')

# Clean up
for spine in ['top', 'right']:
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)

fig.tight_layout()
out_dir = '/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0513_6/projects/faith-evidence-ie/figures/paper'
fig.savefig(f'{out_dir}/fig_evidence_tax.pdf', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=300)
fig.savefig(f'{out_dir}/fig_evidence_tax.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=300)
print('Done. fig_evidence_tax PDF and PNG saved.')

\begin{abstract}

Large Language Model (LLM) based Document-level Relation Extraction (DocRE) now matches or exceeds encoder baselines in extraction accuracy, yet these methods output bare relation triplets without identifying which sentences support each prediction.
Deployment contexts such as clinical knowledge bases and legal due-diligence systems require verifiable evidence that users can trace to source text.
Encoder-based evidence methods (SAIS, DREEAM) provide supporting sentences but trail LLM approaches in accuracy, leaving a gap between extraction performance and output verifiability.

We formalize evidence-grounded DocRE as a structured generation task and compare Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), and Rejection Sampling Fine-Tuning (RSFT) across three fully evaluated scales (1.7B, 4B, 8B) with 14B validation, two model families, and two datasets.
The na\"{i}ve expectation is that evidence generation always costs extraction accuracy. Our experiments reveal that this cost is not fixed but forms a landscape shaped by capacity, paradigm, and data quality. Within the Qwen3 family, evidence is beneficial at 1.7B ($-$5.63pp Ign-F1) but approximately neutral at $\geq$4B (+0.25$\pm$0.47pp at 4B; positive $=$ cost). Gradient-based optimization amplifies evidence-extraction competition (GRPO catastrophic, DPO gradual), while RSFT with Natural Language Inference (NLI) based scoring avoids decoupling entirely through output filtering rather than gradient pressure.

RSFT consistently reduces training seed variance (complete pairwise seed separation on LLaMA, Cohen's $d{=}2.58$; non-overlapping $\chi^2$ CIs at 1.7B). Our 1.7B RSFT model (51.19 Ign-F1, std 0.09pp) approaches 8B Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) performance (50.19, std 3.23pp) at 4.7$\times$ fewer parameters. Test-set evaluation preserves model ranking across all evaluated scales (Spearman $\rho{=}1.0$).

\end{abstract}
